source.title: On Neural Scaling Laws for Weather Emulation through Continual Training
source.authors: Shashank Subramanian; Alexander Kiefer; Arnur Nigmetov; Amir Gholami; D. Morozov; Michael W. Mahoney

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text, including the appendix, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests scaling in weather emulation and finds a regime where extrapolation to a much larger run saturates before the projected validation loss, qualifying the scaling trends. This is a refinement/challenge in a new scientific domain.
record.gate_note: The paper's own weather-model scaling results are recorded. Values from cited NLP scaling studies are not rows. LR choices selected in tuning experiments and comparisons of cooldown versus cosine schedules are not rows for the scaling-law claims.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own IsoFLOP scaling sweep for Swin weather emulators on ERA5 (6E+17 to 6E+19 FLOPs, 3M–456M params). It fits compute-optimal power laws for parameters, samples and loss, then trains an extrapolated 1.3B run at 2.25E+21 FLOPs. This is a new, non-text setting with results on whether the power-law form carries over (V5), so T3 fits better than T5. It does not test language models.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that simple Swin weather emulators trained with constant LR plus cooldowns follow compute-optimal scaling across two orders of magnitude, even with multi-epoch training. The extrapolated 1.3B run shows saturation, likely from limited data and overfitting. They urge scaling analysis before training SciML models at frontier scale, and also claim cooldowns beat cosine schedules and can be repurposed for alignment.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies scaling analysis to weather-emulation Swin Transformers using MSE, ERA5 data, IsoFLOP sweeps, parabolic fits to identify optima, and continual training with constant learning rates and cooldowns. This differs from language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling and its training setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports multi-epoch training and overfitting as relevant to the extrapolated run's saturation. It also reports saturation in extended-horizon RMSE at the highest tested budgets.

fits_no_version.finding: For compute-optimal weather emulators, forecast RMSE up to 240h and high-wavenumber spectral fidelity improve with training compute. Both show signs of saturation at the highest budgets (Figs. 7, 8, 11).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In non-text scientific models, downstream task skill improves with pretraining compute along the compute-optimal frontier.

record.problems: The scaling study is limited to one weather dataset, a deterministic Swin architecture, and a fixed patch size. The largest extrapolated run shows saturation and overfitting. No uncertainty intervals are reported for the scaling fits, and the plotted and appendix validation-loss values for the 1.3B run differ by a factor of ten.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports individual curves in Figs. 7, 8, and 11 and additional case-study outcomes in Figs. 9, 10, and 12. These were not extracted as separate rows because the paper's text summarizes their compute-dependent outcomes without giving separately stated numerical results for each model, lead time, or variable.

untested.parts: All parts: no language models or held-out LM cross-entropy. The weather analogue is recorded under V5.
Extrapolation of LM pretraining-loss laws is not tested. The one weather extrapolation (r4) is recorded under V5.
The LM parameter/token compute-optimal split and the Kaplan vs Hoffmann comparison are not tested. The weather allocation exponents (0.59/0.41) are recorded under V5.
All parts: depth, width and other shape choices are not compared at fixed parameter count. Patch, window and head sizes are fixed.

Image and video models, fine-tuning and transfer scaling, and probabilistic or ensemble weather models are not tested. Only one architecture (Swin), one dataset (ERA5) and a fixed patch size are used.
LM downstream tasks are not tested, and there is no quantitative relation between downstream metric and loss or scale.
Parameter counting, fitting method, schedule and data are not varied to see how fitted exponents shift. Published LM laws are not compared.

missing.what: For the 1.3B extrapolated run, training loss reaches close to the projected loss while validation loss plateaus higher. The fit predicted the training loss but not held-out loss under heavy repetition.
The projected compute-optimal size at 2.25E+21 FLOPs (1.32e9) and the trained size (1310M), showing the run did follow the fitted allocation law.

record.verdict_notes: The versions here are read as LM-scaling claims, with V5 reserved for other domains, so all weather results are linked to V5 only. If V2 and V7 were read as domain-general, r4 would also limit V2 (extrapolation about 37x beyond the sweep fails on validation loss) and would be an instance of V7-style bending. No fit uncertainties are reported. The cosine vs cooldown comparisons, LR selection and alignment-loss results are correctly excluded as method-tuning rather than scaling rows.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses weather-emulation models and MSE, not language models or held-out language-model cross-entropy.
The extrapolation test is for weather emulation, not language models; it tests one extrapolated 1.3B-parameter run rather than multiple larger scales.

The tested allocation is between weather-model parameters and effective (pseudo-)samples, not language-model parameters and training tokens; the study does not compare the Kaplan and Hoffmann allocation laws directly.
The study does not compare depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.

The study tests deterministic weather emulation with a Swin Transformer and continual training. It does not test image or video models, repeated-data regimes beyond its own multi-epoch weather training, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Downstream predictability is assessed for weather-forecast RMSE and spectral metrics, not language-model downstream tasks or a quantitative relation to pretraining loss.

The study reports high-scale saturation and overfitting, but does not systematically vary parameter-counting conventions, fitting method, data, or training schedule to measure their effects on fitted exponents, nor compare published language-model laws.

rows.size_stated: 3M to 456M parameters in the scaling sweep
rows.operation_detail: Sweep model size and training iterations on fixed-FLOP budgets; fit parabolas to IsoFLOP curves to estimate compute-optimal model size.
rows.measure: Compute-optimal parameter count as a function of FLOPs
rows.note: The authors report an optimal model size at each tested compute budget and give the fitted scaling exponent.
rows.check: V3 names LM parameters vs training tokens and the Kaplan/Hoffmann split. This is a weather emulator with multi-epoch pseudo-samples, so it bears on V5 (power-law form beyond text), not V3.

source_check.correct: Section 4 reports N★(C) ∝ C^0.59; Figure 5 gives exponent 0.598. The coefficient appears with a garbled exponent sign in the supplied text; the asserted 2.2252e04 coefficient cannot be accepted as written.
source_check.problem: The coefficient transcription loses an exponent sign and is inconsistent with Figure 5's projected parameter count.

rows.operation_detail: Sweep model size and training iterations on fixed-FLOP budgets; fit parabolas to IsoFLOP curves to estimate compute-optimal sample count.

conditions.value: ERA5; repeated samples treated as pseudo-samples

rows.subject: Swin weather emulator (compute-optimal models)
rows.operation_detail: Fit an empirical power law to compute-optimal validation loss across FLOP budgets.
rows.measure: Compute-optimal validation loss as a function of FLOPs
rows.note: The plotted fit is reported for the weather-emulation setting; the paper does not report language-model cross-entropy.
rows.check: Fig. 5's exponent is printed as C^0.168 but the loss falls with compute, so the fit is L ∝ C^-0.168 (sign lost in extraction). The value should note this.

source_check.problem: The negative exponent sign is inferred from the declining loss relationship; it is missing from the supplied extraction, as the pack acknowledges.

rows.subject: 1.3B Swin weather emulator
rows.operation_detail: Train an extrapolated large run at a compute budget beyond the scaling sweep and compare its validation loss with the projected loss.
rows.measure: Validation loss versus the extrapolated compute-optimal loss
rows.baseline: Projected loss: 0.0033 in Fig. 5; Appendix §A.4 describes the extrapolated loss as 0.033.
rows.value: Fig. 5 labels the 1B run loss as 0.0053; Appendix §A.4 says validation loss plateaus around 0.053.
rows.note: The text says the run saturates before reaching the projected loss and attributes this to overfitting. The displayed loss values differ by a factor of ten between Fig. 5 and Appendix §A.4; both are retained as reported.
rows.check: Bears on V5, since it is weather emulation, not LM extrapolation. V2/V7 are framed around LM laws, so it is removed from them. Fig. 5 gives projected 0.0033 vs measured 0.0053, and the caption says saturated at about 0.005. The appendix's 0.033/0.053 is likely a factor-ten typo. Measured loss is still slightly below the 6E+19 optimum, so partial, not absent.

source_check.locator_found: Figure 5, lines 819–833; §4 (R3), lines 1175–1185; Appendix A.4, lines 1878–1883.
source_check.problem: The row correctly flags the source discrepancy: Figure 5 gives 0.0033/0.0053, whereas Appendix A.4 gives 0.033/0.053.

rows.subject: Swin weather emulator (compute-optimal models)
rows.size_stated: 15.1M to 203.8M parameters among the closest compute-optimal models
rows.operation_detail: Compare validation loss across compute-optimal models in the scaling sweep.

conditions.value: some runs train for more than one epoch

rows.measure: Validation loss and whether it saturates within the scaling range
rows.value: The authors report that the model scales to 6E+19 FLOPs without saturating the loss.
rows.note: This is the authors' stated summary of the tested compute range.
rows.check: Fine. The text has a typo ('6E+19 plots'), meaning FLOPs.

rows.subject: Closest compute-optimal Swin models across budgets
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate forecast RMSE over lead time for compute-optimal models.
rows.value: The authors report that accuracy improves with increased compute and that gains extend to longer forecast horizons.
rows.note: The text summarizes the trend across the compute-optimal models; the figure shows individual model curves.
rows.check: Forecast RMSE of weather emulators is not an LM downstream task. V6 names LM downstream performance, so this is recorded under fits_no_version. It is also a qualitative trend with no fitted relation to loss or compute.

rows.subject: Highest-compute closest compute-optimal Swin models
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate forecast RMSE over lead time at the highest tested compute budget.
rows.measure: RMSE / forecast accuracy at extended lead times
rows.value: The authors report signs of saturation in accuracy for extended forecasts at the highest budgets.
rows.note: The reported saturation is for extended-horizon forecast accuracy, not a claim that all metrics or horizons have stopped improving.
rows.check: Same as r6: extended-horizon RMSE saturation in weather forecasts. This is not an LM downstream result and not a loss-curve fit, so it does not test V7.

rows.subject: Closest compute-optimal Swin models across budgets
rows.operation_detail: Compare prediction power spectral density with ERA5 across compute-optimal models.
rows.measure: Agreement of predicted and target power at higher wavenumbers
rows.value: The authors report gradual improvement at higher wavenumbers with increased compute, with signs of saturation.
rows.note: This is a spectral forecast metric; it is recorded as downstream predictive behavior, not as a language-model task result.
rows.check: Same as r6: spectral (PSD) fidelity of weather forecasts. It is not an LM downstream task.

relationships.condition: Deterministic Swin weather emulators on ERA5, 6E+17 to 6E+19 FLOPs, including multi-epoch runs
relationships.reason: IsoFLOP minima give power laws N*∝C^0.59 and S*∝C^0.41, and compute-optimal loss falls as about C^-0.168. Loss does not saturate in the range (r1, r2, r3, r5).
relationships.display_finding: Compute-optimal allocations followed N*∝C^0.59 and S*∝C^0.41, while loss decreased approximately as C^-0.168 without saturation across the tested range.
